questions.explanation: Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor in the aerobic electron transport chain. It accepts electrons and protons to form water, and this final acceptance permits electron flow through the chain to continue. Therefore, option A is correct; B misidentifies oxygen’s position, C denies its role in permitting continued flow, and D reverses the direction of electron acceptance.

options.text: Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor; it accepts electrons and protons to form water, so aerobic electron flow continues.
Oxygen is not the terminal electron acceptor; it accepts electrons and protons to form water, so aerobic electron flow continues.
Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor; it accepts electrons and protons to form water, but aerobic electron flow cannot continue.
Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor; it donates electrons and protons to form water, so aerobic electron flow continues.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains oxygen’s role at the end of the aerobic electron transport chain?
